summary: Snapshot create/revert/delete owned by a member now converge after a lost or unconfirmed master reply: the owner keeps its local intent (needs_attention with a reason) instead of aborting, re-drives a delete from its journaled target after the master settled it, and spaces re-drives. A restore-as-new definitely refused by the master settles failed and removes its staging.

guide.reason: Operators now see needs_attention with an actionable reason while the owner retries on its own.

api.reason: No endpoint or field changes. The snapshot-reserve and snapshot-settle peer calls and snapshot task results keep their shape; only the owner's handling of an ambiguous reply and of a re-driven delete changes.

roadmap.reason: Bug fixes inside the recovery plan.

state.record: The owner's managed-vms journal and the pool master's VM record (pending_recovery, last_settled_recovery).
state.reason: No new durable state; a fresh Controller reads the same task and VM records from the hosts.

verification.method: Focused Go unit tests in internal/vmhost and internal/agent (in-process master and member over the peer transport, no libvirt, no lab); each new test was shown to fail with its fix reverted.
